rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2014> two-season (2008<U+2013>2009) field experiment at E<U+011F>irdir Fruit Growing Research Station comparing flood irrigation (control) with eight drip irrigation schedules (2 intervals <U+00D7> 4 pan coefficients) on Starkrimson Delicious apple, with own measurements of fruit quality and shoot growth.
rows.notes: The technology matches (transition from flood to drip irrigation), but the study does not report yield. Its own results cover fruit quality (diameter, length, weight, flesh firmness, soluble solids, colour, size-class ratios; Tables 5<U+2013>8) and vegetative growth (shoot number, length, diameter; Table 4), finding drip treatments gave larger fruit, higher extra/class-1 ratios and more shoot growth than flood irrigation. No per-tree or per-hectare yield data are presented, so the passage's claim of yield increases is not supported by this study's own evidence. Fruit weight/size is a quality attribute, not a yield measurement, so this is not treated as an upstream precondition.

notes: Full text appears complete apart from tables and figures not being reproduced; highlights and keywords are empty. The study is a single-site, single-cultivar, two-year trial with no yield outcome.
